target.title: feat(repair): record authoritative dispatch receipts
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/558

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper dispatch lanes could record incomplete request identities, fail outside GitHub Actions, lose cursor progress after a receipt publication failure, or bypass authoritative receipts in the production dashboard Worker. Workflow publication also used the wrong repository credentials and could suppress unrelated activity forwarding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dispatch receipts now bind every transmitted requeue input and support persistent local producer contexts for the documented comment-webhook and executing self-heal commands. Workflow fixes add the sparse state hydrator, use state-repository credentials, keep activity forwarding independent while surfacing ledger failures, and publish fanout checkpoints even when receipt finalization fails.

Both shared dispatch wrappers now treat successful transport as terminal when accepted-outcome receipt persistence fails: the durability failure is logged, chain state is released, and the original sync or async transport result is returned. Attempt creation remains fail-closed, while rejected and unknown transport outcomes retain their existing strict persistence semantics. Target fanout advances its cursor without replaying an accepted dispatch, and the comment webhook returns its accepted response without triggering redelivery.

The setup-action-ledger composite action now exports a canonical `CLAWSWEEPER_ACTION_LEDGER_ROOT` derived from its workspace-relative `worktree-path`, rejecting missing, absolute, or workspace-escaping roots. Executing self-heal therefore receives a valid durable receipt context in GitHub Actions.

The dashboard Worker routes hosted comment dispatch through the ExactReviewQueue Durable Object and records digest-only SQLite attempt/outcome chains for both comment and item repository dispatches. Dispatch input digests reuse the shared action-ledger credential-field validator after the existing flat and size bounds. Raw payloads, comments, prompts, and credentials are not retained.

The branch remains stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/558 so immutable requeue inputs and dispatch receipts share one recovery contract.

## User Impact

Maintainers get an authoritative audit trail for Actions, documented local repair commands, scheduled fanout, and production webhook dispatches. Ambiguous sends remain visible as unknown, accepted sends are not duplicated after receipt persistence failure, successful fanout selection is not replayed, webhook deliveries are not retried after accepted transport, and executing self-heal has a canonical Actions ledger root.

## Evidence

Final head: `24bf3236b94e18b70f1b02a325357b25bdcb616d`

- deterministic sync and async failure injection proves accepted transport results survive outcome persistence failure and dispatch chain state is released
- deterministic target-fanout regression proves cursor progress advances across two accepted sends instead of replaying the first target
- deterministic comment-webhook regression proves accepted transport returns HTTP 202 with one dispatch and no redelivery/report failure
- attempt-write regressions prove sync and async transport remain fail-closed before dispatch
- Actions-context self-heal regression proves attempt and accepted receipts are emitted with the canonical setup-action-ledger root
- credential alias regressions reject `api_key`, `access_token`, `client_secret`, and `password`
- `node --test test/repair/dispatch-action-receipts.test.ts`: 17 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/target-fanout.test.ts`: 10 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/comment-webhook.test.ts`: 30 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/self-heal-recovery-inputs.test.ts`: 9 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/sweep-workflow.test.ts test/repair/command-ops-action-ledger.test.ts test/clawsweeper-action-ledger.test.ts`: 84 passed, 0 failed
- `node --test test/repair/*.test.ts dist/repair/*.test.js`: 801 passed, 0 failed

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram webhook shutdown could leave owned resources active when an early teardown step failed: a synchronous `server.close()` throw, a `bot.stop()` rejection, or a transport-close rejection could skip later cleanup (bot stop, undici transport close, webhook status, diagnostic heartbeat). Ingress-worker `stop()` could also race on repeated calls and leave `worker.terminate()` rejections unobserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Independently guard each ordered webhook shutdown phase via `runTelegramWebhookShutdownPhases` so one sync/async failure cannot skip later owned cleanup, and wrap the path so fire-and-forget abort listeners never leak unhandled rejections. Startup failure cleanup uses `.catch(() => undefined)` so cleanup noise cannot mask the original startup error. Ingress-worker `stop()` shares one in-flight promise and observes terminate rejections.

## User Impact

Operators restarting or aborting a Telegram webhook account no longer risk leaked transports, stale webhook connected status, or leftover diagnostic heartbeats when one shutdown step fails. Process logs no longer see unhandled rejections from webhook/ingress shutdown paths.

## Evidence

Exact head: `115b318a0602120489ca3f2597577e118a16c4ee`

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled|does not skip"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook-shutdown.proof.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```

Observed: 4 webhook shutdown tests passed; proof test passed; 3 ingress-worker tests passed.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: sync `server.close()` throw must not skip bot/transport/status/diagnostics cleanup.
Real environment tested: local Node production-path helper + negative nested-control-flow control (no live Telegram token required for this cleanup contract).

Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/telegram/src/proof-telegram-webhook-shutdown.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=dc6452bf7ea4f208caf64f87c03019d1eeb86d2d

[case 1] negative control — sync server.close throw skips later cleanup
  ok: closeServer ran once
  ok: stopBot was skipped
  ok: closeTransport was skipped
  ok: noteStop was skipped
  ok: stopDiagnostics was skipped
  ok: outer catch logged unexpected error
  info: closeServer=1 stopBot=0 closeTransport=0 noteStop=0 stopDiagnostics=0 errors=1

[case 2] positive control — sync server.close throw continues cleanup
  ok: abort + drain + closeServer ran
  ok: stopBot still ran
  ok: closeTransport still ran
  ok: noteStop still ran
  ok: stopDiagnostics still ran
  ok: server close failure was logged
  ok: shutdown promise did not reject
  info: stopBot=1 closeTransport=1 noteStop=1 stopDiagnostics=1 errors=["webhook server close failed: server close failed"]

[case 3] valid path — clean server.close runs full teardown
  ok: every phase ran exactly once
  ok: no errors logged on clean path
  info: phases_ok=true errors=0

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 15 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control reproduces the pre-fix nested try/finally skip.
- Positive control proves guarded phases continue after sync close throw.
- Valid path proves clean close still runs full ordered teardown.
- Vitest integration: `server.close` monkeypatch on a real started webhook still runs stop/transport/status/diagnostics with no unhandledRejection.

What was not tested: live configured Telegram Bot API gateway restart with a real bot token (cleanup contract is local HTTP + owned transport teardown, not Bot API delivery).

LOC: `extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts` stays at baseline line count (helper extracted to `webhook-shutdown.ts`).
